technical_approach.narrative: Three-phase installation (office wing, main roof Section A, main roof Section B including ponding correction) over 80 days. Max 10,000 sq ft exposed at any time (below RFP 15,000 sq ft limit). Daily watertight close-out. Reinforced tarps for weekend protection. Twice-weekly coordination meetings with facility manager during critical phases. Project Manager Jennifer Morrison (12 yrs), Site Supervisor Tom Bakos (18 yrs), 3 certified roofing technicians (avg 8 yrs).
technical_approach.tear_off_staging_plan: Phased tear-off by roof section: Phase 1 office wing (5,100 sf, days 1-20); Phase 2 main Section A (20,000 sf, days 21-50); Phase 3 main Section B with ponding correction (25,000 sf, days 51-80). Maximum 10,000 sq ft exposed at any time.
technical_approach.weather_protection_plan: Each phase watertight by end of work day; weekend protection with reinforced tarps; specific dry-in plan per phase. No explicit weather-forecast protocol described.
technical_approach.fall_protection_plan: Fall protection training for all workers (updated every 2 years); weekly safety meetings; incident reporting and investigation. No specific anchor-point layout, tie-off strategy for parapets, or CSA Z91-compliant anchor inventory described.
technical_approach.waste_disposal_plan: Visual inspection during removal; work pauses if hazardous materials suspected, pending testing; minor ACM handling included; lead flashings separated and disposed as hazardous waste; daily cleanup and debris removal; legal disposal of removed materials.

wsib_clearance.evidence: Attachments list, page 9: 'WSIB Clearance Certificate' plus 'WSIB Experience Rating Letter (0.89)'. Insurance Coverage section, page 5: WSIB Account #5678901-23.
wsib_clearance.notes: Clearance certificate date not quoted in the bid body. Online re-verification at clearances.wsib.ca will be added as an award condition by the recommendation memo (per fixture 04 §1.4). WSIB experience rating of 0.89 (below industry norm of 1.0) indicates good standing.

cgl_insurance.evidence: Insurance Coverage section, page 5: 'Commercial General Liability: $5,000,000 per occurrence'. COI listed in attachments, page 9. Limit meets RFP §5.1(2) $5M minimum exactly.

Owner must verify these three items on the attached COI before award.

working_at_heights.evidence: Safety Program section, page 5: 'Fall protection training for all workers (updated every 2 years)'.
working_at_heights.notes: Two-year refresh cycle is conservative relative to the O. Reg. 297/13 three-year validity requirement. Ministry-approved WAH training implied though not quoted by regulation name.

labour_material_bond.notes: Same treatment as performance_bond: clarifiable pre-contract, not a submission-stage fail.

red_flags.description: Warranty offered is 20-year membrane-level NDL on TPO only, not total_system_ndl (full assembly: membrane + insulation + flashings + labour to reinstall). RFP warranty_requirements.warranty_type_required = total_system_ndl. Bidder does not attach a named system-warranty program document (e.g., Carlisle Total System, Firestone Red Shield Platinum, Soprema Sopra-Garantie Mammouth Platinum) and the attachment is labeled '20-Year NDL Warranty Sample Documentation' — membrane-level, not system-level.
red_flags.evidence: Warranty section, page 3: '20-year NDL (No Dollar Limit) warranty on TPO membrane'. Attachments, page 9: '20-Year NDL Warranty Sample Documentation'.

red_flags.description: Manufacturer certifications listed are base-tier (Carlisle Syntec 'Certified Installer', Firestone 'Authorized Contractor', Johns Manville 'Preferred Contractor') — NOT the top-tier programs (e.g., Carlisle Perfection Council / ESR, Firestone Red Shield Master Contractor / Platinum, GAF Master Elite, Soprema PAQ+S) whose pre-install review and mid-job inspections are prerequisites to the total_system_ndl warranty tier the RFP requires.
red_flags.citation: fixture 02 §3 (certified installer program hierarchy), §4.5 (total-system NDL prerequisites)

red_flags.description: Wind uplift design basis not stated. Commercial low-slope per OBC Part 3 / CSA A123.21 or FM 1-29 must have a stated wind uplift design. Key Specifications table (page 3) has no wind uplift row; fully adhered method is named without citing the governing uplift calculation or tested assembly.
red_flags.evidence: Key Specifications table, page 3; no wind uplift statement in body of bid.

red_flags.description: Fall protection plan is generic — 'fall protection training for all workers (updated every 2 years)' and 'weekly safety meetings' — with no site-specific anchor-point diagram, tie-off strategy, or parapet/perimeter protection plan for a ~28 ft industrial roof with 47 penetrations. CSA Z91-compliant anchor inventory and specific fall-arrest equipment are not described.
red_flags.citation: fixture 01 §3 (fall protection); O. Reg. 297/13; CSA Z91

red_flags.description: Exclusion item 6 ('Work outside standard hours (7 AM - 6 PM weekdays)') conflicts with the occupied pharmaceutical cold-storage facility. Weekend coverage is described only as passive reinforced tarps; no provision for active emergency weather response outside business hours despite the facility's temperature-sensitive tenant operations.
red_flags.evidence: Exclusions item 6, page 6; Phasing Plan Summary, page 4 (weekend = tarps only).

red_flags.description: Deck repair allowances ($12,000 steel + $8,000 wood) are thin for a 1998 28-year-old BUR tear-off on 85,000 sq ft plus 2006 office wing. Bid does not provide unit prices for deck replacement per board foot or flashing per linear foot, creating change-order exposure for quantities beyond allowance.
red_flags.citation: fixture 03 §3 (allowances vs unit pricing); RFP extraction note on missing wood-deck board-foot allowance
red_flags.evidence: Price Breakdown, page 2; Clarifications item 2, page 6.

red_flags.description: Hazardous materials approach relies on visual inspection during tear-off with no pre-removal testing allowance — 1998 building may contain ACM in BUR asphalt, lead flashings, and mastics. Bidder states 'minor ACM handling included' without defining threshold area or cost cap; major abatement is extra. Owner carries the risk of a work stoppage if ACM is discovered. Owner should obtain a Designated Substance Report per O. Reg. 278/05 before award.
red_flags.evidence: Hazardous Materials Approach, page 5; Clarifications item 3, page 6.

red_flags.description: Manufacturer for base-bid TPO not explicitly committed — bidder lists Carlisle / Firestone / Johns Manville certifications but does not state which manufacturer's system is being installed. This matters because the warranty evaluation and installer-tier check depend on the named manufacturer.
red_flags.evidence: Manufacturer Certifications section, page 6; Key Specifications table, page 3 does not name a manufacturer.

red_flags.description: Permits excluded with estimate '$4,500-$6,000' — typical for Ontario commercial roof replacement but should be carved into the contract clearly (who pulls, who pays) to avoid ambiguity.
red_flags.evidence: Exclusions item 9, page 6; Clarifications item 7, page 6.
